tagline.text: A beach under the forest on Siquijor's east coast, with cliff-jump platforms and clear water

location.label: Location
location.text: Olang, Maria, Siquijor, on the island's east coast

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season, morning high tide

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱100~700 (entrance, parking and gear rental, per person for half a day)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Dumaguete Sibulan Airport (DGT), then a ferry to Siquijor

children.text: Salagdoong Beach lies below the man-made Salagdoong Forest in Maria, on the east side of Siquijor Island. With cliff-jump platforms of different heights and clear water over a seabed scattered with coral fragments, it is a fixture of island-loop itineraries.
Salagdoong Beach is on Siquijor's east coast in Olang, in the municipality of Maria. It is about
30km
from Siquijor town along the coastal road and about
10km
east of Lazi. The road down to the sea runs through a planted forest, Salagdoong Forest, so even the drive in is shaded and pleasant before you reach the water.
The main reason this place is famous is the jump platforms built on the rock cliff. Travel blogs list different heights, but there are said to be two or three platforms between roughly
5m
and

. First-timers should start on the lower one to get a feel for the water depth and the atmosphere before going higher. One side has a concrete deck that is good for resting or jumping, and the other side has fine sand that is good for swimming. The beach floor is covered with small fragments of old coral and shells, though, so it is uncomfortable to walk on barefoot for long and water shoes help. The water is calm and clear with almost no waves, and a coral reef nearby draws many snorkelers. The facilities center on a beach resort run by the local government. It is said to have showers, changing rooms, a picnic area, a small restaurant and air-conditioned rooms. Some reviews say parts of the resort have been closed or under renovation at times, so conditions are not always the same.

It sits close to Cambugahay Falls and Lazi Church on the island-loop day trip, so it is easy to combine them. Many guides suggest arriving in the morning to jump and swim, then heading toward Lazi around lunchtime to see the falls and the church. Early hours are quiet, but from late morning, when tour groups arrive, queues form at the platforms, so timing matters. Maria is a municipality in the southeast of Siquijor with 22 barangays. Olang, where Salagdoong Beach is, is one of the coastal ones, and the church at the town center is dedicated to Our Lady of Divine Providence (Nuestra Señora de Providencia). Rather than only seeing the beach and leaving, a short look at the church and market in Maria town gives you a feel for everyday island life. Taking the reviews together, recent visitors paid roughly
for entrance and
for parking, so a small amount of cash is plenty.

Siquijor is known as the "island of magic," but Salagdoong has nothing to do with that and is a place to enjoy with your body. Planning jumping and swimming in the morning and resting in the shade at midday keeps the day relaxed. If your group includes children or weak swimmers, they can play in the sand on the side opposite the platforms while the adults go to the jump platforms.
The rock cliff has two or three platforms, a lower one and higher ones. Reviews give heights of
5m
7m
8m
and

, so check the exact heights on site. Jumping is included in the entrance fee at no extra charge, but you do it at your own risk. Some reviews say the water is deep enough at the higher platform while others warn it is not very deep, so ask the lifeguards first, starting at the lower platform.

The beach has weak waves and clear water, so it is easy to swim in. The seabed is scattered with coral fragments, so it is not as soft as a sandy beach, but you can see well into the water, which is part of the charm.
A coral reef lies close to the beach, so all you need is a mask and snorkel to get in. Bringing your own gear is the surest option, and whether you can rent some on site varies from day to day.
The planted forest on the road down to the beach forms a tunnel of trees. Riding through on a scooter, the filtered sunlight keeps you cool, and it is a good stretch for photos.
The concrete deck on one side is good for leaving your things, resting and watching the jumpers. A few benches and umbrellas sit on the path behind it, but the spots fill up quickly.
You can eat in the picnic area and rent a beach hut (cottage) by the day. It is convenient for families or groups who want a place to leave their things and rest.
Depending on the season, some places are said to rent kayaks or floats by the hour. The calm water suits beginners nearby, but check on the day whether they are operating.
Set out from your lodging by scooter or tricycle. Ride east along the coastal road and follow the Salagdoong signs down in the Maria section.
Arrive, then pay the entrance and parking fees at the entrance. The quiet early hours are the best time to have the platforms to yourself.
Change into your swimwear, check the water depth and waves from the lower platform, then climb to the higher ones.
Before the tour groups arrive, enjoy the sea by snorkeling or kayaking and rest in the shade.
Have lunch at the beach restaurant or from a packed lunch, then head toward Lazi.
If you have time, continue to Lazi Church and Cambugahay Falls. In that case it is better to finish the beach in the morning.
High tide changes every day. If you want to jump, check the tide table before leaving and time your visit to high tide.

items.title: Island-loop day course
items.subtitle: From the beach to the falls and the church

children.text: Start from Siquijor town or Larena port and ride clockwise along the coastal road.
Jump and swim at Salagdoong Beach.
Move on to Lazi and have lunch.
Cool off at
Cambugahay Falls
and look around
Lazi Church
The loop is long by scooter and takes some stamina. Allow plenty of time so you are back at your lodging before dark.
Fly from Manila to Dumaguete (DGT) on a direct flight, then transfer to a ferry from Dumaguete port to Siquijor. Check the operator's latest announcements for ferry fares and schedules.
After you land at a Siquijor port (such as Larena), rent a scooter or find a tricycle and head for the beach.

items.title: From the port to the beach

children.text: Renting a scooter and riding yourself is the most common way. Daily rental fees differ by review at
. From Siquijor town or San Juan it takes about
30–60 minutes
along the coastal road.
A tricycle needs negotiating because the distance is long and the fare is high, and reviews mention about
one way. Agree on the waiting time as well.
From Lazi it is about
15–20 minutes
to the east.
It is often included in island-loop tours (with Cambugahay Falls and Lazi Church), so look into that to fit your schedule.
The dry season from November to May is best for sea activities. During the day, the morning through early afternoon is best, when the waves are weak and there are fewer people.
Many reviews say cliff jumping is best at high tide. Check the tide table and plan to arrive around high tide.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Best season for jumping and snorkeling; more people around the New Year
Warm, clear water, but shade at midday and sun protection are essential
Platforms may be closed when waves or rain are heavy, so check on site

The beach resort is run by the local government and is said to have air-conditioned rooms, but I could not confirm room rates. One review says from about ₱1,000, but this changes, so ask before booking. Most travelers stay in Siquijor town or San Juan and visit as a day trip.

There is a small restaurant at the beach and shops nearby selling snacks. Many reviews say prices are higher than in town supermarkets, so it helps to bring water and snacks. If you plan to eat in the picnic area, you have to prepare your own food.

If you want to stay into the evening, Lazi and San Juan have more dining choices. Paliton Beach on the west side of the island is popular for sunsets, and reviews also recommend riding the day loop clockwise and ending in the west.
To jump, go early in the morning or on a weekday. From late morning, when tour groups arrive, queues form at the platforms.
Arrive around high tide. Check the tide table before leaving and ask the lifeguards first whether jumping is possible.
The beach floor has many coral and shell fragments, so water shoes help.
Bring a waterproof case, sunscreen, a change of clothes, a towel and snorkeling gear. Carry plenty of cash as well.
Combining Cambugahay Falls and Lazi Church in Lazi as part of an island-loop day trip makes your travel more efficient.
Wear a helmet and ride a scooter safely. The coastal road is generally in good condition, but be careful in the village sections.
If you are in a group, have one person watch the bags and phones and take turns jumping. I could not confirm whether the beach has lockers for valuables.
If you want to film your jump, strap a waterproof case or action camera to your wrist. It is hard to find if you drop it in the water.
Warm up before jumping, and get in the water first to feel the temperature and current. It is much safer than suddenly jumping from a high platform.
If your schedule is tight, set aside at least two or three hours for jumping and swimming. Including photos and rest, reviews put it at two to four hours.
Cliff jumping is at your own risk. Always jump feet first, not head first, and check the water depth and the lifeguards' signal.
Platform heights and water depth differ by source. Practice on the lower platform before moving to a higher one.
Do not jump when the sea is rough or when it is raining. The resort may also close the platforms.
Never jump after drinking. Serious injuries may have to be transported as far as Dumaguete.
Parts of the resort may be under renovation or closed. Check the latest announcements or confirm on site.
Entrance fees and opening hours differ by review, so I could not confirm exact values. Check with the local tourism office or on arrival before you visit.
Weak swimmers and children should stay away from the platforms and play only on the shallow sandy side.
About
20–30 minutes
toward Lazi, this waterfall pairs well with the island-loop course.
A church with a long history, worth a stop with the falls when you look around Lazi.
